answer: Stake-bonded identity is a concrete Sybil defense: each agent locks real value as a bond before it may vote or earn rewards, and a trellis of smart contracts binds one bond to exactly one identity. To fake a thousand participants in the orchard, an attacker must lock a thousand separate bonds, so the cost rises linearly with every fabricated agent rather than staying flat. Any agent caught double-voting is slashed, driving its capital to the nadir and destroying the stake. Honest agents simply reclaim their bond, so only fraud is punished and a Sybil flood becomes unaffordable.
